stem:
Neil's rhombus has diagonals $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ and $24\ \mathrm{cm}$. Each side is $13\ \mathrm{cm}$.

Which claim correctly finds the area?

options.text: Area $=\tfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times 24=120\ \mathrm{cm}^{2}$, using the product of the diagonals.
Area $=10\times 24=240\ \mathrm{cm}^{2}$, treating the diagonals as base and height.
The side $13\ \mathrm{cm}$ is what produces the diagonals $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ and $24\ \mathrm{cm}$ as an area step.

teacher.key_rationale: Rhombus diagonals are perpendicular, so area is half their product: (1/2)×10×24=120. Dropping the half, using side×side, or reversing side and diagonals as an area step all miss the diagonal-product reasoning.
